title: A Night at the Night Market
passage:
Last Friday, Ben and his sister Lucy went to the night market near their house. The market was more crowded than usual because of the summer festival.

"Look at that line!" Lucy said. "The fried chicken stall is the most popular one here."

"Let's try the stinky tofu first," Ben said. "It smells strong, but it tastes amazing."

They walked past rows of stalls selling grilled squid, bubble tea, and sweet potato balls. The smell of spicy sauce filled the air.

At one stall, an old vendor was selling handmade bags. "These bags are cheaper than the ones in the department store," the vendor said with a smile.

Lucy wanted to buy a small bag, but she didn't bring enough cash. "Can you lower the price a little?" she asked. The vendor laughed and gave her a small discount.

Ben was too hungry to wait in the long line, so they chose a quieter stall instead. He ordered a bowl of noodles, and Lucy got a cup of mango shaved ice.

"This is the best shaved ice I've ever had," Lucy said happily.

Before going home, they stopped by a game stall. Ben tried to win a prize by throwing rings, but it was harder than it looked. In the end, they just laughed and decided the fun was more important than the prize.

It was a noisy, crowded, and wonderful evening. Both of them agreed that the night market was definitely worth the trip.

vocab.example: The night market opens every evening after six o'clock.
The night market gets very crowded on weekends.
She bought a scarf from a small stall near the entrance.
The vendor sold fresh fruit juice at a low price.
My mother always bargains with vendors at the market.
We got a ten percent discount on the shoes.
The sauce was too spicy for my little brother.
Grilled squid is one of the most popular snacks here.
The street was noisy because of the loud music.
The taste of the stinky tofu was amazing.
That bubble tea shop is the most popular one in town.
He won a small prize by playing the ring toss game.
This is definitely the best night market I've visited.

grammar: 比較級與最高級 (Comparative and Superlative Adjectives)：形容詞比較用法，如 more crowded than（較級，多音節加 more...than）、cheaper than（單音節加 -er）、the most popular / the best（最高級，表示「最...」）。
too...to 句型：「too + 形容詞 + to + 動詞」表示「太...以至於不能...」，如 too hungry to wait（太餓了以至於無法等待）。

reading.q: Why did Lucy ask the vendor to lower the price?
reading.ex: 文中提到 Lucy 想買小包包，但「didn't bring enough cash」（沒帶足夠現金），所以才請小販降價。

reading.q: Why did Ben and Lucy choose a quieter stall for food?
opts: The fried chicken stall was closed.
Ben was too hungry to wait in line.
The vendor gave them a discount.
reading.ex: 文中寫道「Ben was too hungry to wait in the long line, so they chose a quieter stall instead.」，因為 Ben 太餓了等不了，所以選了排隊較少的攤位。

reading.q: What did Lucy say about the shaved ice?
opts: It was the best she had ever had.
reading.ex: Lucy 說「This is the best shaved ice I've ever had.」，表示這是她吃過最好吃的剉冰。

reading.q: What happened when Ben played the ring toss game?
opts: It was harder than he expected.
reading.ex: 文中提到「it was harder than it looked」，表示遊戲比看起來的更難。

reading.q: How did Ben and Lucy feel about their evening at the night market?
reading.ex: 文末寫道「the night market was definitely worth the trip」，表示他們認為這趟夜市行很值得。

grammar.q: The night market was ______ than usual.
grammar.ex: crowded 是多音節形容詞，比較級須用「more + 形容詞 + than」，故選 more crowded。

grammar.q: This is ______ shaved ice I've ever had.
grammar.ex: 表達「我吃過最好的...」要用最高級，前面須加 the，故選 the best。

grammar.q: These bags are ______ than the ones in the department store.
grammar.ex: cheap 是單音節形容詞，比較級加 -er，故選 cheaper。

grammar.q: Ben was ______ wait in the long line.
grammar.ex: 「too + 形容詞 + to + 動詞」表示「太...而不能...」，故選 too hungry to。

grammar.q: It was ______ game than he expected.
grammar.ex: hard 是單音節形容詞，比較級加 -er，故選 harder。

vocab.ex: stall 指市場或夜市裡的「攤位」。
bargain 作動詞時表示「討價還價」。
spicy 表示「辛辣的」，味道嗆辣。

vocab.q: The street was very ______ because of the loud music.
vocab.ex: 因為音樂很大聲，所以街道是「吵鬧的」，故選 noisy。
vendor 指在市場或路邊販賣商品的「小販」。
